title: a member whose only declaration is in the standard library still needs an adapter when it is read off a foreign value, because the declaring file was never the question
notes:
specification/compatibility.mdx, 'Foreign Boundary' (Locked): 'Calling an unannotated foreign runtime value MUST add the checked `panic` case, because JavaScript and TypeScript may throw, reject, or violate a declaration.' `constructor` is declared in `lib.es5.d.ts` and nowhere in the imported module, so a rule that decides by asking where the member is DECLARED admits this read; nothing whatever stops a foreign object from serving `constructor`, `length` or `toString` from a throwing getter or a `Proxy` trap, and `lib.es5.d.ts` is a description of a shape, never a trust claim about a particular object. This case and 09-foreign-calls/a-foreign-index-signature-read-through-an-element-access-needs-an-adapter are the two halves of the same argument: a member with NO declarations, and a member whose declaration is in a file the author is inclined to trust. Asking the receiver one question answers both. The receiver here is `spreadable`, whose own `a` getter throws, which is what makes the object a real hazard rather than a hypothetical one.

2026-09-07 retirement: measured as XPASS in the full native-only corpus run. The native boundary reporter now charges Panic to the enclosing row before inference, so both profiles report the complete authored diagnostic list, including VIBE1101. No source, required code, position or message assertion was removed.
